planting.note: Direct sow in fall or plant divisions in spring into moist, humus-rich soil at a woodland edge in part shade to shade; bastard balm needs cold stratification to germinate well from seed.

directions: Plant in part shade to shade at a woodland edge in moist, humus-rich soil; bastard balm is a European woodland relative of balm and mint bearing white-and-pink, orchid-like flowers in late spring over honey-scented foliage. It was historically used as a wound herb and remains valued today chiefly as a strong bee- and pollinator-attracting shade perennial. Give it the dappled light and steady moisture of a woodland garden edge, where it naturalizes well without becoming aggressive, and divide congested clumps in spring every few years.

planting.note: Direct sow or plant divisions in spring into lean, sharply drained soil in full sun; False Dittany needs excellent drainage and resents winter wet more than cold.

directions: Plant in lean, sharply drained soil in full sun; False Dittany is a Cretan and Aegean subshrub with thick, scalloped leaves covered in dense white felt, grown chiefly as a silver-foliage accent for a dry Mediterranean border or rock garden. It was historically used medicinally much like true dittany (Origanum dictamnus) for wound care and digestive complaints, though today it is grown primarily for its ornamental felted texture. It is drought-tolerant once established and performs best where winter soil stays on the dry side, since excess moisture is more damaging to it than cold alone.

planting.note: Direct sow or plant divisions in spring into dry, rocky, calcareous soil in full sun; this is a distinct species from the already-present Sideritis scardica and S. syriaca.

directions: Plant in dry, rocky, calcareous soil in full sun; Sideritis raeseri is one of the classic Greek mountain tea ironworts (known locally as tsai tou vounou), traditionally harvested from Mt. Olympus and brewed as an everyday herbal tea valued for digestive and anti-inflammatory use. Soft, gray-fuzzy foliage covers upright stems to about 18 inches, topped by the characteristic yellow whorled flower spikes typical of the genus. It is extremely drought-tolerant once established and needs little care beyond good drainage and full sun exposure.
sources: Kreta24 specialty Greek herb seed house

planting.note: Direct sow or plant divisions in spring into sharply drained, gritty soil in full sun to light shade; Pyrenean germander is very slow-growing and best suited to a rock-garden crevice.

directions: Plant in sharply drained, gritty soil in full sun to light shade; Pyrenean germander is a mat-forming alpine herb from the Pyrenees bearing tiny aromatic leaves and distinctive bicolor purple-and-cream flowers in summer, holder of a Royal Horticultural Society Award of Garden Merit. Like other germanders it was traditionally used for bitter digestive tonics, though today it is grown mainly as a choice rock-garden and trough plant. It is very slow-growing and needs sharp drainage above all else; avoid rich or consistently wet soil, which quickly rots the roots.

planting.note: Direct sow or plant divisions in spring into dry, rocky, well-drained soil in full sun; mountain germander forms a low creeping mat and makes a tough, drought-tolerant groundcover.

directions: Plant in dry, rocky, well-drained soil in full sun; mountain germander is a low, creeping subshrub native to Mediterranean and sub-alpine rocky ground, bearing tiny fragrant leaves and creamy-white flowers through much of summer. In Balkan folk tradition it was brewed as a bitter digestive and anti-inflammatory tea, similar to other germander species already in cultivation. It makes an excellent dry rock-garden groundcover, spreading slowly to knit together gravel or scree plantings, and needs essentially no supplemental water once established.

planting.note: Direct sow or plant divisions in spring into lean, well-drained soil in full sun; silver horehound is grown chiefly as a felted silver-foliage accent rather than a kitchen herb.

directions: Plant in lean, well-drained soil in full sun; silver horehound is a Balkan relative of common horehound (Marrubium vulgare) carrying felted, scalloped, silvery-gray leaves and whorled white flowers in summer. It is grown primarily as an ornamental silver-foliage plant for a dry border or gravel garden, though like its common cousin it has traditionally been used for cough and throat remedies. It is extremely drought-tolerant once established and needs little care beyond good drainage, avoiding rich or consistently damp soil.

planting.note: Direct sow or plant divisions in spring into lean, sharply drained soil in full sun; wild savory is a strong bee plant as well as a culinary herb.

directions: Plant in lean, sharply drained soil in full sun; wild savory is a small aromatic Mediterranean subshrub native to Spain, Portugal, Morocco, and Greece, used in light herbal teas and as a savory-like culinary seasoning for meats and legumes. Its tiny flowers are heavily favored by bees, making it a worthwhile addition to a pollinator-focused herb garden as well as the kitchen. It is drought-tolerant once established and makes a good low, aromatic filler for a dry rock garden or gravel path edge.

planting.note: Direct sow or plant divisions in spring into lean, sharply drained soil in full sun; desert wormwood is adapted to true arid-steppe conditions and resents rich or regularly irrigated soil.

directions: Plant in lean, sharply drained soil in full sun; desert wormwood is a dwarf shrub of North African and Levantine semi-arid steppe, a key traditional medicine plant across the region used for digestive complaints and in folk diabetes management, with documented antimicrobial activity in ethnobotanical literature. Its finely divided, silvery-gray aromatic foliage makes it a striking dry-garden or xeriscape accent beyond its medicinal history. It is extremely drought-tolerant and performs best in lean, mineral soil, declining in rich or consistently moist conditions.
sources: Ethnobotanical literature on North African medicinal plants

planting.note: Direct sow or plant divisions in spring into lean, sharply drained soil in full sun; this close cousin of curry plant (Helichrysum italicum) carries the same curry-scented foliage.

directions: Plant in lean, sharply drained soil in full sun; shrubby everlasting is native to southwestern Europe and northwest Morocco, forming a compact cushion shrub with the same distinctively curry-scented silver foliage that makes the related Helichrysum italicum popular, along with small, long-lasting 'everlasting' flower heads valued in dried arrangements. It has been used in folk remedies for skin and respiratory complaints much like its better-known cousin. Extremely drought-tolerant once established, it needs lean soil and sharp drainage to avoid winter rot.
